prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Choose Your Pet Style Preset", "Select a base style direction to ensure your custom pet generates smoothly on your desktop."]
1: ["Summoning Your Companion to Desktop", "Your pet is being built and prepared to roam your screen."]
2: ["Desktop Pet Controls & Shortcuts", "Right-click your pet anytime to chat, change settings, or send it to the system tray.", "Got It, Bring Pet Out!"]
3: ["Sign In to Save & Restore Your Pets", "Your existing pet profiles and desktop companion data sync automatically upon sign in."]
4: ["Signing in automatically restores all previously created pets and customization progress."]
5: ["Adopt Your Desktop Companion in Under 1 Minute", "Pick a pet, customize its look, and watch it walk across your desktop instantly."]
6: []
7: ["We'll notify you when your pet is ready on your desktop so you can safely switch windows."]
8: []
9: ["Tip: Right-click your pet on desktop or use the system tray icon anytime to access controls and chat."]
